Three is the integer preceding four and following two. Three is also the first odd prime number.

History[edit]

The earliest representations of three used three individual strokes (III), a method common in Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, and early Brahmic scripts where the lines were aligned vertically. During India's Gupta Empire, curves were added to the lines. The Nāgarī script later rotated these lines horizontally and added a short downward stroke on the right, which eventually connected in cursive writing into a symbol like ३. The Indian numeral system spread to the Islamic world in the 9th century. By the 10th century, Western Arabic regions (like the Maghreb and Al-Andalus) dropped the bottom stroke to form the ancestor of the modern Western 3, while Eastern Arabic scripts retained and rotated the stroke to form ٣.Pythagoras called 3 the first true number and a symbol of completeness representing a "beginning, middle, and end".
